text:
Vegas won this one on special teams, not on the run of play at five-on-five. Mitch Marner scored on the power play at 2:40 of overtime, a snap shot that Mark Stone and Trevor Connelly set up, and it settled a game in which both teams' power plays scored on chances worth less than a fifth of a goal apiece. VGK went 2 for 3 with the man advantage on 0.40 expected goals; LAK went 1 for 3 on 0.51.

The second period was where the game tilted. VGK out-chanced LAK 1.50 to 0.32 in expected goals, and Connelly opened the scoring at 2:37 with a power-play snap shot. Artemi Panarin answered at 6:21, also on the power play, with a wrist shot off assists from Adrian Kempe and Brandt Clarke. The first period had been close (0.73 for LAK, 0.64 for VGK), and the third was nearly even again (0.51 for VGK, 0.49 for LAK). Overall VGK held the edge in chance quality at 2.81 to 1.91, and even strength widened it to 2.4 to 1.3.

Connelly carried the most weight, with a goal, an assist and six shots on goal while VGK's on-ice expected goals were 1.1 to 0.05. Carter Hart stopped 26 of 27 shots, 0.91 goals better than the chances deserved. At the other end, Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves on 32 shots and was 0.81 goals above expected. The simulated replays give VGK the win 66 percent of the time. Here the better side got it, though it took overtime and a power play to finish.
